newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bearish Brent heading for $17.61 support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bearish Brent heading for $17.61 support.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ Brent failed its upside test at $18.77 last week and this now casts a bear's shadow over the markets.
+ Next support lies at $17.61 and a break of that will lead to numbers as low as $16.47 over the next couple of weeks.
IPE Brent crude oil futures lay under the shadow of a bearish market top and are likely to turn downwards, traders and technical analysts said on Tuesday.

June Brent closed 31 cents down on Friday at $17.97 a barrel, after testing, and failing to break above, the top of a key chart gap at $18.77. May gas oil fell a dizzying $4.75 to close at $165.50. The IPE was closed on Monday because of a U.K. holiday.
"The market failed to fill the gap to $18.77 and we are now looking for a retest of the lows and to take out support at $17.61," said Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Derivatives.

"I expect that to be taken out in the next two or three days," he said, adding that this would lead towards $16.47, a number calculated by taking the width of the range $17.61-$18.77 and subtracting it from $17.61.
The market was likely to work towards that price in the coming weeks, he said.
In the shorter term he said he saw temporary suport at $17.81, representing the short term low point on the June contract chart on April 23.
Gas oil, he said, would play a similar game to Brent, although its historical chart had shown more volatility.

Resistance at $172.50 for the May contract "should keep a lid on it," Wilson said, adding that support would be found at $162.75, then $161.75, followed by $159.75, the low of last month's trading range.
A break below that would herald a move towards $147.00, calculated as the $159.75 low minus the width of the previous trading range.
Peter Sceats at CharTech-MCS was less bearish in the short term but in the longer term he was negative too.

"On balance one has to stay with the current 'side to up' trend for short term positions but with the weight of the down trend bearing on the market be more than wary as to what can happen if this trend support is broken.
While he pegged strong resistance at $18.77, he saw support at $17.61.
"The $17.61 tough low will be seen by many as the last bastion of support for this version of the price action."
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
